email.subject: Re: Day-old markdown timing, from October 9
email.body:
Ines Thorvald said on October 9, in the bakery day-old pricing conversation: "Day-old loaves go to half price at two in the afternoon, not at close. At close nobody is left to buy them." Caleb Ruiz answered in the same exchange: "Then the shelf card changes at two as well, so the price is never a surprise at the till."

Day-old loaves now mark down at two, and the shelf card changes at the same hour, so the price on the shelf and the price at the till agree. The reasoning Ines gave is that the discount only does work while buyers are still in the shop. Nothing in the conversation says whether the card is changed by hand or by the till system, and nothing says what happens on a day the bakery runs short of day-old loaves before two.

That suggests to me that the close-time markdown is no longer the rule, so nothing needs to be built around a closing-hour price. I read Caleb's line as the part that now needs a check: if the card is changed by hand, someone has to be at the shelf at two, and the closing staff are where a missed change would show first. If that holds, the two o'clock time becomes the one thing the staff keep in mind.

Two questions remain open. Does the two o'clock change hold for the closing staff too? Who changes the shelf card, and is it done in the same minute as the markdown?
